html:
The Panama hat is a brimmed hat woven by hand from the leaves of the toquilla palm in Ecuador, especially around Montecristi and Cuenca. It got its name because it was shipped and sold through Panama.

Weaving these hats is an old craft of the coast of Ecuador. In the 1800s they became a major export, worn by workers in the California gold rush and by labourers on the Panama Canal. A photograph of Theodore Roosevelt wearing one at the canal works in 1906 made them fashionable.

The finest hats, woven over months, can be rolled up without damage. Hats were at times among the country's leading exports, shipped by the merchants of Guayaquil. In 2012 UNESCO listed the weaving of the toquilla straw hat as intangible heritage of humanity.
